items.briefing:
Attackers are now using calendar invite files (.ics) to deliver phishing attacks — these look like legitimate meeting requests but can direct you to malicious links when opened. If you receive an unexpected calendar invite, especially from an unknown sender, be cautious before clicking any links inside it.

A Canadian man has pleaded guilty over extortion attacks targeting organisations using the Snowflake cloud platform, a reminder that cloud data storage can be a target if credentials aren't properly protected. **Practical tip:** Be wary of unexpected calendar invites — if in doubt, verify the sender directly before accepting or clicking any links.
